Question:
Billy’s basketball team scored the following points over the course of the first \(11\) games of the season:

\(42,\) \(47,\) \(53,\) \(53,\) \(58,\) \(58,\) \(58,\) \(61,\) \(64,\) \(65,\) \(73.\)

If his team scores \(40\) in the \(12\)th game, which of the following statistics will show an increase?
Solution:
The new score, \(40\), becomes the smallest score. Check how this changes each statistic.

The range is the largest score minus the smallest. It increases from
\[
73-42=31\quad\text{to}\quad73-40=33.
\]
The original median is the sixth score, \(58\). After inserting \(40\) at the beginning, the sixth and seventh scores are both \(58\), so the new median is also \(58\).

The mode remains \(58\): it still occurs three times, more than any other score.

The original scores total \(632\). Thus the mean decreases from
\[
\frac{632}{11}=57\frac{5}{11}
\quad\text{to}\quad
\frac{632+40}{12}=56.
\]
The mid-range is the average of the smallest and largest scores. It decreases from
\[
\frac{42+73}{2}=57.5
\quad\text{to}\quad
\frac{40+73}{2}=56.5.
\]
Only the range increases, so the answer is \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
